{{Short description|Algebra of possibly unbounded operators}}
In [[mathematics]], an '''O*-algebra''' is an [[Operator algebra|algebra]] of possibly [[unbounded operator]]s defined on a dense subspace of a [[Hilbert space]]. The original examples were described by Borchers (1962)<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Borchers |first=H. -J. |date=April 1962 |title=On structure of the algebra of field operators |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF02745645 |journal=Il Nuovo Cimento |language=en |volume=24 |issue=2 |pages=214–236 |doi=10.1007/BF02745645 |issn=0029-6341|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and {{harvtxt|Uhlmann|1962}},<ref>{{Citation |last1=Uhlmann |first1=Armin |title=Über die Definition der Quantenfelder nach Wightman und Haag |journal=Wiss. Z. Karl-Marx-Univ. Leipzig Math.-Nat. Reihe |volume=11 |pages=213–217 |year=1962 |mr=0141413}}</ref> who studied some examples of O*-algebras, called [[Borchers algebra]]s, arising from the [[Wightman axioms]] of [[quantum field theory]]. Powers (1971)<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Powers |first=Robert T. |date=June 1971 |title=Self-adjoint algebras of unbounded operators |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF01646746 |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |language=en |volume=21 |issue=2 |pages=85–124 |doi=10.1007/BF01646746 |issn=0010-3616}}</ref> and Lassner (1972)<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lassner |first=G. |date=December 1972 |title=Topological algebras of operators |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0034487772900122 |journal=Reports on Mathematical Physics |language=en |volume=3 |issue=4 |pages=279–293 |doi=10.1016/0034-4877(72)90012-2|url-access=subscription }}</ref> began the systematic study of algebras of unbounded operators.
